name: Fetal Lung Interstitial Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Fetal Lung Interstitial Tumor

criteria.description: Presence of spindle-shaped interstitial cells with bland nuclei and abundant myxoid stroma on histopathology
Prenatal or neonatal imaging showing a well-circumscribed, solid lung mass without cystic components
Immunohistochemical positivity for vimentin and negativity for epithelial markers
Presentation in the perinatal period with respiratory distress or asymptomatic lung mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of spindle cell proliferation with supportive imaging findings and immunohistochemistry
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily histopathological; prenatal imaging aids early detection.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prenatal detection of solitary solid lung mass
searchTerms: single solid lung lump before birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological identification of spindle cell proliferation in lung interstitium
searchTerms: fibrous cell growth in lung biopsy

common.symptomName: Asymptomatic lung mass detected incidentally postnatally
searchTerms: lung mass found after birth without symptoms

common.symptomName: Reduced breath sounds over affected lung
searchTerms: decreased breath sounds in lung area
less air movement detected in lung
shift of chest structures on imaging

occasional.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to respiratory compromise
searchTerms: feeding problems due to breathing issues

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypoplasia secondary to mass effect
searchTerms: pulmonary hypoplasia due to lung mass

rare.symptomName: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
searchTerms: persistent high blood pressure in lungs of newborn
lung blood vessel pressure problems after birth

imaging: Prenatal ultrasound or MRI showing solitary, well-circumscribed solid lung mass
Postnatal chest X-ray or CT demonstrating homogeneous lung lesion without cystic changes
genetic: No recurrent genetic mutations identified; tumor considered sporadic
other: Histopathology showing spindle cell proliferation with myxoid stroma
Immunohistochemistry positive for vimentin, negative for epithelial markers

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cystic lung lesions on imaging
Aggressive malignant tumor with cystic and solid components
Histopathology showing blastematous and sarcomatous elements
Often presents later in infancy or childhood

redFlags: Severe neonatal respiratory distress requiring ventilation
Rapidly enlarging lung mass on imaging
references: Dehner LP et al. Fetal lung interstitial tumor: a newly recognized lung neoplasm of infancy. Am J Surg Pathol. 2010.
Yousem SA et al. Pediatric lung tumors: a review. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2015.
